title: fix: unblock upgrades with retired JSON state
body:
Fixes #174343

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the update dead end where pre-July JSON state makes current Doctor or update admission require an intermediate release that cannot complete the operator's repair.

## User Impact

Operators can run current `openclaw doctor --fix` and continue upgrading. Doctor imports legacy cron definitions/runtime state, referenced OAuth credentials, Voice Wake settings, conversation bindings, and default-home plugin approvals into existing SQLite owners. Current SQLite data wins, and original bytes are preserved in named archives.

Obsolete delivery queues, plugin indexes, sandbox registries, replay ledgers, and restart notifications are archived with recovery instructions. Old deliveries are never replayed automatically. Doctor tries both historical OAuth key files and, in an interactive terminal, the existing macOS Keychain entry; missing keys leave archived ciphertext and give `openclaw models auth login --provider openai` as the forward path. Restoring archived sources does not replay a completed credential import.

## Why This Change Was Made

Importer removal left refusal guards as the only owner of several shipped state formats. The base [refusal at lines 37–40](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5aec205816506ceb6983a5ab1c549c9e0b301a61/src/infra/state-migrations.retired-files.ts#L37-L40) still directs operators to 2026.9.7. Source history identifies removals in `ff96d47c3506` (delivery queues), `a8c1182c16eb` (cron), `d12a2cf036c5` (OAuth sidecars), `f77ceef31812` (pre-June OAuth), and `3543c6bb0895` (runtime JSON).

Restore the shipped parsing logic under Doctor's existing maintenance and migration owners, and reuse the existing verified backup/receipt owners for archival. Runtime readers stay on current formats. Admission keeps importable user-state sources pending until current Doctor has committed them, and refuses sources it cannot inspect; transient archives remain advisory. Config-only recovery retains the guard against discarding a custom cron locator before its source is imported; its recovery action is current Doctor. No schema, dependency, or public option changes.

The simplification removes obsolete refusal paths and refusal-only tests. The remaining growth is the one-shot import logic needed to repair every refused category together. A binary archive regression also fixes a shared verifier that hashed decoded UTF-8 instead of original bytes. The historical OAuth reader only tried its first key-file candidate; Doctor now tries both existing locations without adding an environment option. Missing sidecars leave the auth source pending so correcting a stale locator and rerunning Doctor still recovers the credentials. Unattended runs preserve the existing no-Keychain-prompt contract.

## Evidence

### Latest two-red recheck (head d21351a9)

Both remaining failures are inherited on current `origin/main` (`f6f939a8ebc65fc9bbe6c01b6723677e94a9614f`). The newer CI merge is `22791d7d0d6af6cf8cc09d05e010716f5c43efbf`, combining this PR with main `571eaa2a5927295874564af075ba99015a57cc6b`. This Matrix failure is distinct from the earlier missing-receipt failure recorded below.

| Check | Current comparison | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bun Doctor model check | Current-main exact file: 13 pass / 1 fail, 38.75s wall; the same unexpected `openrouter/openrouter/auto` advisory. | The inherited OpenRouter static catalog classification issue remains. |
| PostgreSQL Matrix roots | Exact unchanged file: 3/3 `promise resolved { phase: 'preflight', ... } instead of rejecting` failures on both plain main and this PR cleanly merged with the same main in a temporary checkout. Main 41.37s Vitest / 47.81s wrapper; PR comparison 46.38s / 53.98s. | Main commit `a1bdebdb9f8dec868e069700f39422f36ad81e22` correctly makes roots with zero legacy inbound-dedupe rows port-ready. The fixture creates only canonical `idb-snapshot` chunks, but its shared setup still expects the earlier one-time-scan refusal added by `f2478e569a15`. |

The Matrix detector, portability test, and port-preflight owner are byte-identical between the two comparison trees and between CI's main base and current main. This failure occurs at the shared fixture's initial dry-run assertion, before its Doctor repair block or any port publication. No retired sources were archived or reclassified by this PR to produce the result.

Commands used fresh isolated HOME/OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/cache directories. Doctor: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-src.config.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Matrix: `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:32771/postgres -- src/infra/database-engine/matrix-roots.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The owned local PostgreSQL container used CI's pinned pg17/pgvector image and was removed afterward. No test assertion, baseline, or production code was changed.

The unchanged Matrix detector regression also passed on the PR/current-main combination: a fresh snapshot root returns no migration, then adding a real legacy inbound-dedupe row reports pending migration (725ms test; 30.94s Vitest including preparation). This verifies that actual legacy rows retain their blocking semantics.


### CI repair and exact-source comparison

CI run 38943317928 tested merge `016a42a64cf09519fa463161d5d58b3e38f34f4c`, combining PR head `0cb58fb83e3211a545b00b73544c758366fca124` with main `7e1e6cfc4e18528de2dd3a897049d5f860742ddc`. Comparisons below use the original PR head, that exact merge where newer-main tests are involved, and an untouched detached `origin/main` at `b4569473a552d5dc10f8ce2f19d0084b449d7dc0`. Every command used a separate HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, and test cache under this worktree's `.artifacts/`.

| Reported check | Attribution | Reproduction and repair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check-lint-core-1` | Ours | The exact core stripe commands (1/5 and 2/5) reproduce `typescript(no-unnecessary-type-conversion)` in `legacy-oauth-sidecar.ts:336`. Plain main lacks that new conversion. Removed the redundant Boolean call. The corrected stripe has no remaining finding in either changed file; focused lint with `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` passes. Local strict line-limit findings in untouched files are inherited; 16 affected paths also fail on current plain main and another older main path has since been refactored. Hosted CI reports these limits as warnings. No rule, limit, or baseline changed. |
| `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` / database-worker | Ours | Original branch fails with two unreviewed credential-writer references to `importConfigMachineState`; plain main passes. The batch import can select the credential row, so the guard correctly requires a reviewed caller. Replaced the Voice Wake calls with the existing scalar atomic updater using literal noncredential keys and keep-current-or-import callbacks. The exact ratchet now passes (`222 → 222` T1 calls and `12 → 12` compatibility calls); no guard exemptions or baseline changes. |
| PostgreSQL / `matrix-roots.postgres.test.ts` | Inherited, fixed on main | The test and port-preflight owner do not exist on the original PR branch (the explicit test selection reports no files). The exact CI merge reproduces all three failures: pending inbound-dedupe scan receipt, then `0` instead of `2` publication calls on resume/rollback. None of these owners differs from CI's main parent. Plain main passes 3/3 with existing fix `f2478e569a150583622632387fe616f23eb833fc`, which repairs the fixture through the registered Doctor migration before porting. |
| Bun compact-small-9 / Doctor model check | Inherited | Original branch passes. The CI merge and plain main both reproduce the same unexpected `openrouter/openrouter/auto` advisory. Main commit `eaaf5533213de19e614689d7b5bdb539d05fa92b` added static Jev rows, causing model-reference validation to treat the runtime-discovered OpenRouter catalog as exhaustive. This PR did not change the test or model-validation owner. |
| Bun compact-small-3 / session worker control | Inherited, fixed on main | Original branch passes all 12 worker-control cases. The exact CI merge reproduces the missing-notice assertions and 120-second waits. Main's `47edda1e4d2294826fff66c0a3d41defff768354` changed runtime-config lookup, exposing the fixture's missing accepted store resolver. Current main passes all 12 with existing fix `f527f20f741d00183ece27517f4f0a20db1a1b6d`. |

Exact static commands: `node --import tsx scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mts --only=core --split-core --core-stripe=1/5 --threads=1`, followed by stripe `2/5`; `node --max-old-space-size=4096 --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-database-worker-ratchet.mts --base 7e1e6cfc4e18528de2dd3a897049d5f860742ddc`.

Exact Bun comparison: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-src.config.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.test.ts src/sessions/session-state-events.worker-control.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Original branch: 26/26 pass, 56.46s wall. Plain main: 25/26 pass with only the inherited model assertion, 66.07s wall. Source preparation took 30.445s and 33.9s respectively.

Exact PostgreSQL comparison: `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:32770/postgres -- src/infra/database-engine/matrix-roots.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Used CI's pinned PostgreSQL 17/pgvector image in an owned local container, removed afterward. Main: 3/3 pass, 194.97s Vitest / 207.46s wrapper (cases 64.722s, 53.192s, 20.897s). CI merge: all three failures, 87.08s Vitest / 101.97s wrapper; the tests themselves used 24.711s. This existing real port/backup/recovery suite is slow; no timeout or assertion was weakened.

The exact CI-merge Bun replay completed with the original nine failures (the Doctor model assertion and eight worker-control failures), 17 passes, and 424.09s wall time. The three worker waits each reach the existing 120-second timeout because the missing resolver prevents the fixture's deferred operation from starting. Current-main worker cases finish in milliseconds; neither timeouts nor assertions were changed here.

Post-fix proof: all 16 direct/barrel-import affected test files passed (352 tests; five selected shards in 391.17s), including all four runtime SQLite rejection/source-retention/retry regressions and canonical-value preservation. Core tsgo, touched-file type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and madge (0 cycles) passed. The exact full core stripe replay now has only inherited untouched line-limit findings. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defect. This follow-up is production +12/−4, with no new test code; existing failure/retry regressions cover the changed contract.


Live revalidation on committed `d21351a9f6911f993ee7f7c5d845d7e236ce2c9d`: used `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_HOME=.artifacts/l1650/ci-live-home`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` at its `.openclaw`, explicit config/profile selection, and synthetic port 62947. No Gateway was started. `pnpm openclaw --profile l1650-proof update admit --context <synthetic-context.json>` exited 3 and all 20 fixture files remained byte-identical. `pnpm openclaw --profile l1650-proof doctor --fix --non-interactive` exited 0 (`Doctor complete.`). Verification found 19 exact-byte archives and committed cron, Voice Wake, conversation binding, plugin approval, and both OAuth credentials. Final admission exited 0 with `verdict: admit`, empty reasons, and empty warnings. The build completed from the committed source.

### Persistence-failure repair

The follow-up fixes a data-loss path in the restored cron/runtime importers: a catch covered both rejected JSON and SQLite errors, then source cleanup ran. The shared retired-state owner now parses separately from persistence. Only intentionally rejected input or a completed commit lets an importable source reach archival. SQLite load/write failures retain live sources, propagate a visible failed step, and keep admission refused with `openclaw doctor --fix` guidance. Successful archive warnings are advisory; lock and persistence failures remain blocking.

- Reproduction on `f86ebb0c`: five new cases failed (four runtime import failures and a cron SQLite-load failure). Final regressions also inject a real cron write rejection inside its transaction; sources remain byte-identical, no rows are committed, and clearing the fault lets a rerun import and archive them. Malformed-input and current-value preservation cases pass.
- All 14 affected sibling files passed (392 tests); after the final parser cleanup and successful-step classification, the two owning files passed again (13 tests). Core and changed-test typechecks, direct oxlint/oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and the import-cycle check passed (0 cycles). Final independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. No timeouts or assertions were weakened. The final 13-test run took 74.67 seconds wall time, dominated by compilation; the runtime file reported 95% transform and 2% test time.
- Live proof on committed `0cb58fb83e32`: explicit `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_HOME` at `.artifacts/l1650/followup-live-home`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` at its `.openclaw` directory, matching `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=l1650-proof` and explicit `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, with isolated port 56188. In an authority-free child environment, `pnpm openclaw --profile l1650-proof update admit --context "$PWD/.artifacts/l1650/live-admission-context.json"` exited 3 for the actual legacy sources; all 20 fixture files remained byte-identical. `pnpm openclaw --profile l1650-proof doctor --fix --non-interactive` then exited 0 (`Doctor complete.`). Verification found 19 byte-exact archives plus the migrated cron definition, Voice Wake setting, conversation binding, plugin approval, and OAuth credential. The same admission command then exited 0 (`admit`). The initial harness attempt was rejected for inherited supervisor metadata; an empty-profile probe was discarded and repeated with explicit profile/config selection. Neither was counted as migration proof.
- OAuth audit: the existing receipt owner verifies persisted credentials before archival, and import/commit/verification errors preserve both auth sources and referenced sidecars. It remains separate from the generic archive helper. Delivery queues, plugin indexes, and sandbox registries intentionally archive transient bytes without SQLite import; state-directory migration relocates the preserved tree.
- Simplification shares cron source enumeration and parse/commit/archive ordering, reuses number normalization, and deletes redundant parser/inspection code. The still-active runtime/plugin-index refusal shells were retained. This follow-up is production +172/−174 (net −2) and tests +222/−29; no schema, dependency, public option, or baseline changes.


- Real CLI, isolated synthetic HOME/state/profile: `pnpm openclaw --profile l1650-proof doctor --fix --non-interactive` exited 0 with `Doctor complete.` Verified 19 retired originals were removed only after byte-identical archives existed; cron definition/runtime state, both synthetic OAuth profiles, Voice Wake settings, bindings, and approvals were present in current SQLite. The recovery capture manifest existed before repair.
- Same isolated state: `pnpm openclaw --profile l1650-proof update admit --context <synthetic-context.json>` exited 0 with `{"verdict":"admit","reasons":[],"warnings":[]}`. No operator state or existing Gateway was used.
- Untouched-base comparison at `5aec205816506ceb6983a5ab1c549c9e0b301a61`: all seven new cron/OAuth cases fail at the retired-source refusal. The repair fixtures cover plaintext/encrypted OAuth, stale-primary/valid-fallback keys, unavailable keys, malformed cron data, and preservation of canonical data and source bytes.
- Exercised all 213 selected affected-consumer test files across scoped runs. After the final corrections, the four affected suites passed all 72 tests (124.54s in Vitest; 265.30s including preparation). The missing-sidecar retry, plaintext/encrypted/fallback-key imports, byte-identical archives, config-only cron protection, and verified-account session routing pass.
- Core typecheck, changed-test typecheck, direct oxlint/oxfmt, four-page MDX check, line-cap ratchet, import-cycle check, and `git diff --check`: passed. Final independent review was scoped-clean through P2. Runtime and E2E builds completed successfully.

Known inherited proof limitations: unchanged `src/state/openclaw-state-ownership.test.ts` reports fixture lock handles remaining open after cleanup (16 teardown failures in the affected run; the untouched base reproduces the same signature, with a 22-test cleanup cascade). The existing daemon-runtime-pin maintenance-lock release is the narrow suspect; the exact retained resource remains unproven. The environment-name check reports 453 against budget 452 on both the base and this patch; no budget was changed. Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was omitted because its SQLite inventory stalls on this host; PR CI remains the broad proof. No remote lease was used.

The separate npm-manifest symptom did not reproduce: updating a legacy npm record for the published `@openclaw/brave-plugin@2026.10.1` succeeded despite its manifest ID being `brave` (`Updated brave: 2026.9.7 -> 2026.10.1`). No installer change is included. Source history does not establish which historical release resolved the reporter's npm failure; the broader reported environment-specific staging failure remains unconfirmed.

Production LOC: +1450 / −338 (net +1112). Test LOC: +982 / −522. Documentation: +74 / −62.
